subsystems.name: Receiver and spectrometer
subsystems.role: turns the telescope's voltage stream into high-resolution time–frequency power spectra.

subsystems.name: Interference excision
subsystems.role: removes obvious terrestrial transmitters before any search begins.
parts: masks for known satellite, radar and GPS bands

subsystems.name: Candidate search
subsystems.role: classical narrowband drift search that finds peaks with a near-constant drift rate.
parts: candidate table with frequency, drift rate and time

subsystems.name: Training-set generator
subsystems.role: creates labelled examples, since no confirmed technosignature exists to learn from.
parts: grid of signal-to-noise ratios and drift rates

subsystems.name: Classifier
subsystems.role: ranks spectrogram patches as signal-like or interference-like.

subsystems.name: Cadence and RFI validator
subsystems.role: tests whether a candidate behaves like something on the sky rather than something local.

subsystems.name: Human review and follow-up
subsystems.role: astronomers inspect the top-ranked candidates and re-observe the best ones.

buildSteps.title: Record the sky
buildSteps.detail: Observe target stars in a cadence that alternates ON-source and OFF-source pointings over hundreds of megahertz to a few gigahertz, saving channelized voltages or spectra at high time and frequency resolution.

buildSteps.title: Form dynamic spectra
buildSteps.detail: Convert the raw data into calibrated dynamic spectra — frequency on one axis, time on the other — correcting the bandpass and flagging saturated or transmitter-dominated channels.

buildSteps.title: Run a classical search first
buildSteps.detail: A dedoppler drift search finds narrowband peaks, allowing for drift rates of a few hertz per second caused by the Doppler shift of a moving transmitter. This produces a candidate list that can run into the millions per observation.

buildSteps.title: Inject synthetic signals
buildSteps.detail: Add artificial drifting carriers of known strength and drift rate into real recordings, and label them alongside patches of genuine terrestrial interference. This builds the balanced training set that a real technosignature would otherwise provide.

buildSteps.title: Train and validate the network
buildSteps.detail: Train a convolutional or transformer model on spectrogram patches, holding out data for validation and always scoring the classical algorithm on the same set as a control, so any gain from machine learning is measurable.

buildSteps.title: Score live candidates
buildSteps.detail: Apply the trained model to new observations, re-ranking the candidate list so that signal-like patches rise to the top and interference-like ones drop away, cutting the volume a human must inspect.

buildSteps.title: Check the observing cadence
buildSteps.detail: A genuine sky signal should appear when the telescope points at the target and vanish when it points away, and should recur at the same drift rate on later visits. Interference usually does neither. Failing this test eliminates most remaining candidates.

buildSteps.title: Review and re-observe
buildSteps.detail: Astronomers examine the surviving candidates and, for the most promising, request confirming observations with other telescopes or interferometers to localise the source and rule out local interference.

prerequisites.why: narrowband searches need fine frequency channels over wide bands, which is what modern radio telescope backends provide.
spectrogram data from long surveys is too large to review manually and is what makes learned classifiers worthwhile.
it supplies the candidate list the model re-ranks and the baseline against which any improvement is judged.
positively labelled examples must be synthesised or borrowed from interference, because no extraterrestrial technosignature has ever been confirmed.
only a second instrument, or an interferometer that gives a sky position, can show a candidate is not local interference.

pathway.milestone: learned classifiers re-ranking candidates from surveys of thousands of nearby stars, as published from Green Bank Telescope and FAST data
pathway.unlocks: human review effort focused on a small fraction of candidates.

pathway.milestone: real-time inference at the telescope, so low-value data is discarded before it is stored
pathway.unlocks: surveys of the galactic centre and nearby galaxies at volumes today's pipelines cannot handle.

pathway.milestone: common candidate formats and automated alerts that trigger follow-up on other telescopes within hours
pathway.unlocks: confirming or eliminating a candidate before interference conditions or the source's position change.

pathway.milestone: commensal machine-learning searches running continuously on next-generation arrays and cross-matched with optical and infrared surveys
pathway.unlocks: a search that covers the sky rather than a list of targets, with multi-wavelength evidence for anything found.
